P-06 Booking order and payment

Bangla name: বুকিং অর্ডার ও পেমেন্ট

← 20 · User portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Booking and payment. The heart of the business: the customer confirms the selection of P-04, the platform checks the rules, locks the capacity, creates a Pending order with a server-computed price, sends the customer to the DgePay payment page, and, when DgePay reports back, marks the order Paid and starts everything that follows (capacity deduction, VAT challan, ticket creation). If payment does not arrive in time the order is cancelled and the seats are released (S-05).

2. Trigger and actor

Signed-in customer with a completed profile (the server refuses otherwise), pressing Purchase on the seats page and confirming in the payment pop-up (CompletePaymentModalComponent). The payment itself happens on DgePay's hosted page.

3. Business flow

  1. The pop-up repeats the choice (event, seats, price) and offers Pay; pressing it disables the button while the request runs.
  2. The browser is redirected to DgePay (window.location.href = checkoutUrl); the customer pays by their method.
  3. DgePay tells the platform the result; the platform then sends the customer's browser back to the portal (the configured DgePay:RedirectUrl), which shows the booking list (P-07).
  4. A Paid order gets tickets; the customer asks for the final signed tickets later (P-08).
  5. If the customer abandons the page, nothing is charged; the Pending order and its seat lock expire after about 12 minutes.

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] POST {services.bookings}/booking/api/v1/user-booking-order with TicketPurchase (P-04 §4 step 6) (BookingApiService.ticketPurchase; server [Authorize(Policy = User)]). UserBookingOrderManager.CreateAsync:
  2. loads the caller's profile from the identity API (userClient.GetUserAsync(), [HTTP, static key]); no profile or IsProfileCompleted false → Complete your profile first!;
  3. takes the Redis lock user_booking:{userId} (60 s); not acquired → Simultaneous order is prohibited. Try again later.;
  4. loads the event through the Event client; not published or not active → This event is currently unavailable for booking.;
  5. ValidateBookingOrderCreate: gallery, block, level ids > 0; seats > 0; PricePerSeat > 0, TotalCharge > 0, Vat ≥ 0 (client values, only checked for sign); NumberOfSeats ≤ AllowableMaximumSeatPerOrder; the level's gallery, block and level must exist, be active and sellable, and match the sent ids (unauthorized_access otherwise); selling window (ticket_selling_is_not_started_yet, ticket_selling_stopped); order_limit_exceeded and seat_limit_exceeded from the customer's earlier orders (see note 5);
  6. for seated levels: the requested seats must all be in the live free-seat list, else Unavailable seats: ...;
  7. generates a unique order number {TicketNumberPrefix}{code};
  8. takes the lock level_booking_{event}_{gallery}_{block}_{level} (60 s, waits up to 15 s) and calls CapacityManager.BookLevelCapacity (locks the seats/amount for 12 minutes in the Redis hash level_locked:*; live capacity is reduced only after payment, S-01);
  9. computes the price on the server from the event settings (VAT inclusive or on top, percentage or fixed), the level price, the system discount (Discounts table), the promo code (P-05) and the platform (service) charge; stores Vat, Discount, PromoDiscount, PlatformCharge, TotalCharge, status Pending, a new PaymentTransactionId (GUID), OneIdUserId from the profile;
  10. stores one BookedUserRecords row per ticket (the holder names and phones sent, empty rows for the rest);
  11. asks DgePay for the checkout link (InitiateDgePayPayment) and returns { publicId, checkoutUrl } with HTTP 201. The gateway choice code (ResolvePaymentGateway, SSLCommerz) is commented out: every order uses DgePay (Q-19).
  12. [HTTP, static/encrypted] → DgePay: DgePayPaymentManager.InitiatePaymentAndGetCheckoutLink authenticates (/payment_gateway/authenticate, Basic client credentials), AES-encrypts the body (amount, transaction id, callback URL DgePay:CallbackUrl) and posts to /payment_gateway/initiate_payment; the answer's WebViewUrl is the checkout link. Any failure returns null (logged only).
  13. The customer pays on DgePay. DgePay then calls [HTTP, no token] GET /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order/dgepay/payment-status?data=<AES-encrypted> (anonymous). HandleDgePayment decrypts the data, finds the order by UniqueTxnId, and: - status Paid and order younger than 12 minutes: publishes [SQS: OrderSuccess] (level capacity update, S-01), sets the status, stores the callback text and time, calls Ticketing initiate-user-ticket (creates the ticket rows, S-07) and publishes [SQS: VatChallanProcessing] (S-10); - status not Paid: deletes the order from the locked-capacity hash; - order older than 12 minutes: the status and the capacity message are not applied (the order is left for the background cancel); the callback text is still stored. The code after that point does not look at the age: for a Paid callback it still calls initiate-user-ticket (which refuses because the order is not Paid, logged as a warning) and still publishes the VAT challan message [UNCONFIRMED: Q-15]. The action then always answers with a 302 to DgePay:RedirectUrl, even if processing failed (errors are only logged).
  14. Background: orders still Pending after the callback window are re-checked against DgePay (check_transaction_status) and cancelled if unpaid (S-05).
  15. Portal after redirect: the portal route tickets (without language) redirects to /{savedLanguage}/tickets (P-07); no payment result is passed in the URL, the list reads the status from the server.
  16. Test/bypass path: GET /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order/payment-status-bypass?rawData=<order public id> is anonymous, does not ask DgePay, forces Paid with the text "BY PASS TRANSACTION - TEST", publishes OrderSuccess and initiates tickets (X-18; this is the critical finding of the review).

Method Path Auth Request Response Main errors

GET /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order/dgepay/payment-status anonymous (DgePay callback) data (encrypted) 302 to DgePay:RedirectUrl none returned
GET /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order/payment-status-bypass anonymous rawData (order public id) 302 none returned

7. Data and side effects

UserBookingOrders (Pending, later Paid), BookedUserRecords, seat lock in Redis, DgePay session, then (after payment) SQS messages, ticket rows in Ticketing, a VAT message and capacity changes. The activity log records the order changes (X-24).

9. Handover notes

  1. Anyone who knows an order's public id can mark it paid. payment-status-bypass is anonymous and permanent in the code; it also starts ticket creation. Remove it or protect it before production use (X-18). Locally it is a handy way to simulate a payment (§11).
  2. The checkout failure is invisible to the customer. If DgePay does not return a link, checkoutUrl is null; the portal only acts when a URL exists, so the pop-up stays in the loading state with no message (loading is not reset).
  3. A paid order after 12 minutes is lost to the platform. A late DgePay callback neither updates the status nor deducts capacity; the money may have been taken while the order is cancelled by the background job (S-05, [UNCONFIRMED: Q-11]).
  4. Two customers choosing the same seats: the first order takes the lock; the second fails with Unavailable seats: ... or a capacity message (P-04 note 2). A refused purchase keeps its seats locked until the 12-minute lock expires [UNCONFIRMED: Q-37].
  5. Limit checks are loose. order_limit_exceeded fires only when the customer already has more than AllowableMaximumOrderPerUser orders (so one more than the limit is possible), and seat_limit_exceeded compares all seats the customer ever booked for the event plus the new ones with the per-order maximum AllowableMaximumSeatPerOrder, so that setting works as a per-customer total as well [UNCONFIRMED: Q-38].
  6. The server price can differ from the preview (P-04 note 1); the amount charged is TotalCharge as computed in step 8.
  7. No "resume payment". The endpoint that would regenerate a checkout link for a pending order is commented out in the controller (UserBookingOrderController.cs:287); a customer who closes the DgePay page must buy again.
  8. The callback trusts the encrypted message. HandleDgePayment takes the status from the decrypted data (shared AES key) and does not call check_transaction_status; only the background re-check does (S-05). Protect the key like a password (X-26).
  9. Always a redirect. A failure while processing the callback is logged as critical and the customer is still sent to the portal, where the order shows Pending until the re-check.
  10. Error messages from the server are shown as text (err.error.title); machine codes such as ticket_selling_stopped or order_limit_exceeded are displayed as they are unless the portal translates them [UNCONFIRMED: Q-39].
  11. Profile call per order. Each order calls the identity API; if it is down the customer cannot buy (Complete your profile first! is also the message for a missing profile).

11. Developer test guide

Local testability: Partial. DgePay is a dummy locally, so the real payment page and callback cannot run; the order creation and the capacity lock can.
